newsitem.title: USA: Nets Inc seeks extra finance, not ready for IPO.
newsitem.headline: Nets Inc seeks extra finance, not ready for IPO.

text.p: Internet commerce firm Nets Inc on Monday said it was seeking additional investors as it refocuses on its maintenance and repair market plans, but is not ready for an initial public offering (IPO) yet.

"I don't think its a secret that we're seeking additional investors, but there is not going to be an IPO anytime soon," a spokeswoman said, adding that more work was needed to prepare the company for a public offering.
Nets on Thursday told employees that it would be cutting 54 of its 304 posts, and closing down its AT&T Business Network new media service.
Nets bought Business Network from AT&T last June for a nominal sum, but the spokeswoman said it had already been effectively wound down in operational terms.

Nets, whose biggest shareholders include former-Lotus Development Corp chief executive Jim Manzi, is planning to build a business-to-business electronic commerce operation to help maintenance and repair organizations buy parts.
In an e-mail to staff, made available to Reuters, Manzi said that the company expects to at least double revenue in 1997 and gain at least 200,000 new customers.
He also said the company would phase out of its target marketing business.

If it is successful serving the market for industrial components in areas like air conditioning and heating, it will replicate its approach in new markets, Manzi's e-mail said. It did not give figures for 1996 revenue or customers.
